comments.body:
**Should fix** — short-row message counts file lines, which the parser has already joined

The summary says a short row "usually means a line was cut off in the file" and gives a line number. The check runs after `csv.reader` has joined quoted line breaks, and a row is one parsed record, not one line of the file (T-010), so the line number can point past the row it names. As worded, someone reading the log opens the file at the wrong line.

<details><summary>Standard</summary>

key: `term/T-010/widgets/loader.py::_report_short_rows`
</details>

🤖 _AI-assisted comment, reviewed and approved by @alice before posting._
comments.author: alice

comments.body: Agree. The log should talk about parsed rows; a line number from the file sends people to the wrong place.
comments.author: alice

comments.body:
Fixed in 3e5a1c2. The summary in `_report_short_rows` no longer gives a file line number. It now names the row by its index after parsing and says a row spans several lines of the file when a quoted field holds a line break. The same string goes to the `UserWarning` and the log.

🤖 _AI-assisted comment, reviewed and approved by @alice before posting._
comments.author: alice

comments.body:
**Should fix** — a new public constant and warning ship as a patch

This adds a public module constant (`ROW_LIMIT`) and a new `UserWarning` from `load_rows`, but the version moves 2.4.0 -> 2.4.2 and the body says "Public signatures: none". A consumer pinned with `~=2.4.1` takes a patch silently, and one running with warnings as errors would fail on it. This should be the next minor version, with the `## 2.4.2` changelog heading to match.

<details><summary>Standard</summary>

key: `R-012/pyproject.toml::version`
</details>

🤖 _AI-assisted comment, reviewed and approved by @alice before posting._
comments.author: alice

comments.body: Disagree. Nothing callers rely on changes here: `ROW_LIMIT` is informational and the warning fires only on files that were already malformed, so a patch release is right. 2.4.1 is reserved for the fix queued ahead of this one.
comments.author: alice

comments.body:
**Suggestion** — long-row message says every long row is a delimiter error

`n_long` also counts rows with a trailing delimiter, repeated header rows, and rows whose quoting the dialect does not recognise. When short rows are present, "this usually means the delimiter is wrong" overstates the errors. The message could say the count includes those cases.

<details><summary>Standard</summary>

</details>

comments.author: alice

comments.body: Agree. The count mixes several causes, and the message should list them instead of guessing one.
comments.author: alice

comments.body:
Fixed in 9b04d7e. The long-row log now says what the count includes: rows with a trailing delimiter, repeated header rows and rows whose quoting the dialect does not recognise, as well as true delimiter errors. It also says `ROW_LIMIT` is a first guess and tells the reader to compare the count with the short-row count before reading it as delimiter errors. The exact-string assertion in `test_report_short_rows_logs_long_rows_without_warning` is updated to match.

comments.body:
**Suggestion** — no case for a short last row with no trailing newline

The parametrize covers a short row and a file with no trailing newline separately, but not a short last row with no newline after it, e.g. `"a,b,c\n1,2"`, which should classify as one short row. It does today; one more `pytest.param` here pins that the two cases hold where they meet.

**Suggestion** — nothing tests that `summary_only`/`verbose` reach the helper

AC-5 is tested only on `_report_short_rows` directly. Dropping `summary_only=summary_only, verbose=verbose` from this call leaves the suite green, so the public function's documented quieting is not enforced. A `load_rows` case with `summary_only=True` on a file with short rows would cover it.

comments.body:
Fixed in 51c8f0a. There is a new test, `test_load_rows_passes_summary_only_and_verbose_to_report`, parametrized over `summary_only=True` with `verbose` False (expects 0 per-row lines) and True (expects 1). Dropping `summary_only` from the call fails the first case, and dropping `verbose` fails the second.

**Question** — can the upstream export write a blank row between sections?

If it can, a blank row is labelled by the dialect: with `skipinitialspace` it reads as one short row, without it as no row at all. Whoever owns the export could answer this, and say what `ROW_LIMIT` should be.
